newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to inject $18.1 mln in 2M TV capital.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to inject $18.1 mln in 2M TV capital.

text.p: Morocco's television 2M, which recently ceded 70 percent of its stake to the state, said on Monday it plans to increase its capital by 158 million dirhams ($18.1 million) by end 1996.

In a news conference held at the television headquarters on Monday evening, managing director Larbi Belarbi said "in line with the company's new strategy...We plan to increase the capital of 2M television by 158 million dirhams by end 1996".
Belarbi gave no details of 2M's present capital.

Earlier this year the government said it would pay 100 million dirhams for the 70 percent controlling interest in the loss-making television station, owned by the private SOREAD company (Societe d'Etudes et de Realisations Audiovisuelles).
SOREAD is a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group.
Officials said 2M had made losses totalling 455 million dirhams ($52.2 million) and the private group shareholders could no longer afford to keep it running.
"It is now a question of survival...We have to succeed because a television which does not succeed will die," Belarbi told reporters.
Casablanca-based 2M, is a pay television with an average 100,000 subscribers with decoders in Morocco's main cities.
Belarbi said the television broadcast will be extended to 70 percent of Morocco's 27 million population "with no charge" starting from January 10, 1997.
No decoders will be needed to receive 2M's programmes in future, he added.
Morocco has a public television (RTM) located in Rabat which broadcasts to the whole territory, including the disputed Western Sahara under Moroccan administration.
